title: The shape after a chain of movement ops
prompt: Given a starting shape and a list of movement ops, write shape_after(shape: list[int], ops: list[Op]) -> list[int], the final shape. The ops are small dataclasses. Reshape(shape) and Expand(shape) give the new shape directly, Permute(order) reorders axes, Pad(pads) adds a left and right amount per axis ([l0, r0, l1, r1, ...]), and Reduce(m) drops the first m axes. The inputs are always valid.
hints: Loop over the ops and replace shape with the shape after each one.

A match with one case per class reads cleanly. case Reshape(s) | Expand(s): handles both ops that name the new shape outright. Permute picks shape[p] for each p in the order. Pad adds pads[2*k] and pads[2*k + 1] to axis k.
Reduce(m) drops the first m axes, which is the slice shape[m:].
explain: Movement ops never look at the data, so a shape is enough to type check a whole chain. Each op is a small function of the old shape, and applying them left to right gives the final one.
